newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's LPMO buys 10,842 tonnes of frozen beef.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's LPMO buys 10,842 tonnes of frozen beef.

text.p: South Korea's Livestock Products Marketing Organization (LPMO) said on Thursday it had bought a total of 10,842 tonnes of frozen beef in two days of tenders last Friday and on Tuesday.
An LPMO official said it bought 5,866 tonnes of Australian beef, 3,490 tonnes of U.S. beef, 1,162 tonnes of Newzealand beef and 324 tonnes of Canadian beef.
U.S. and Canadian chuck roll was bought at $2,865-$3,307 per tonne, knuckle at $3,443-$3,695 a tonne and short-rib at $2,889-$3,430.
Australian and New Zealand grain-fed bone-in beef was bought at $2,417-$2,521, grass-fed fullset at $2,893-$3,127 and grass-fed bone-in beef $1,764-$1,915.
The LPMO had originally invited tenders for 10,860 tonnes of beef but bought 18 tonnes less due to high prices.
Arrivals were set for Seoul, Pusan, Taegu and Naju. Shipment of 2,481 tonnes was slated for November 10, 4,703 tonnes for November 20 and 3,658 tonnes for November 30.
